[Listen on Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/start/id1790754910)[Listen on Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/show/1CHxZLMn9OqIMbuOKOkJ9j?si=4e1cb38b027e4134)[Watch on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@tryfondo)[Subscribe to START](https://tryfondo.beehiiv.com/subscribe)


‍


Generating more leads won't help much if your sales team doesn't know which ones to call.


A prospect engaging with a competitor might be evaluating alternatives.


Someone discussing a specific business problem might be looking for a solution.


A visitor landing on your website might be researching a purchase.


Each interaction can be useful.


But none of them automatically makes someone a qualified buyer.


That's the problem Roman Czerny and his team are addressing with GojiBerry.


Instead of asking salespeople to build prospect lists from scratch, GojiBerry uses an AI agent to identify buying signals and qualify potential customers.


It can monitor engagement with competitors, track discussions around relevant keywords, and incorporate website visitor signals.


Then it evaluates which prospects fit the company's target customer profile.


Once qualified, GojiBerry can create personalized outreach and run automated LinkedIn and email campaigns.


Sales teams receive notifications when prospects respond and can continue conversations directly through Slack.


The goal is to spend less time identifying potential buyers and more time speaking with the right ones.


Roman shared an example of a customer that now books 60% of its demos through GojiBerry.


Rather than having salespeople create arbitrary prospect lists, the team uses GojiBerry to identify qualified leads and then calls those prospects directly.


What's interesting is that Roman applies a similar philosophy to GojiBerry's own growth.


The company publishes practical customer acquisition guides, distributes them widely, and then identifies qualified prospects among those who engage.


The content generates attention.


The qualification process determines where the sales effort goes.


Roman says the resulting interest has grown to the point that the company doesn't have enough salespeople to contact everyone.


It highlights an increasingly important distinction in sales.


**Finding people is getting easier. Knowing which people are worth contacting is where the real value lies.**


More leads aren't necessarily the answer.


Better information about which leads to pursue can be far more useful.
